publication.book: Principles and Practice of Interventional Pulmonology

diagnostic_approaches.name: BAL instillation volumes and aliquots
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Obtain diagnostic samples from alveolar spaces for cellular and microbiologic analysis.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Instill sterile isotonic saline via bronchoscope in wedge position or via distal catheter.
limitations: Technique parameters are not fully standardized across centers
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: During bronchoscopy when BAL is indicated.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: The minimum is considered about 100 m L of lavage fluid in adults. The recommendations reach from 100 to 300 m L for BAL and aliquots of 20–50 m L

diagnostic_approaches.name: BAL recovery volume interpretation
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Assess adequacy and interpretability of recovered BAL sample.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: 30–70% recovery is expected; 5% may still be adequate for analysis.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Immediately after BAL to judge sample adequacy.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: A recovery of 30–70% of the instilled volume is normal. The minimum is at 5%, which is adequate for analysis.

diagnostic_approaches.name: BAL site selection using imaging
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Optimize diagnostic yield by choosing sampling site.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Target middle lobe or lingula for diffuse disease; target area of greatest abnormality on radiograph/CT for localized lesions.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: About 20% more fluid/cells recovered from middle lobe/lingula than lower lobes.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: From these lobes, about 20% more fluid and cells are recovered than from the lower lobes.

diagnostic_approaches.name: BAL differential cell counting method
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Standardize enumeration of BAL cell types.
criteria_or_scoring: Count at least 600 cells on stained preparations.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Use cytocentrifuge/cell smear; stain with May-Grünwald-Giemsa; exclude ciliated/squamous cells from differential.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: ≥600 cells improves reproducibility and lowers variability of differentials.
limitations: Diff-Quick should not be used because it does not stain mast cells.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Routine BAL cellular analysis in ILD evaluation.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: For the enumeration of cell differentials, at least 600 cells are counted on cytocentrifuge or cell smear preparations

diagnostic_approaches.name: Flow cytometry cell requirement for BAL
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Ensure adequate cellularity for reliable BAL flow cytometry.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Quantify total cells prior to flow cytometry; proceed only if threshold met.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Below this threshold, flow cytometry may be inadequate.
limitations: indicated with high lymphocyte counts or suspected specific entities.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When immunophenotyping lymphocyte subsets or suspected LCH/lymphoma.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: The crucial point for flow cytometry is that ≥1 × 106 cells are required to perform an adequate test.

diagnostic_approaches.name: BAL sample contamination criterion (epithelial cells)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Assess sample representativeness for diffuse parenchymal disease.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Note ciliated or squamous epithelial cells and exclude from differential count.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: High epithelial cell percentage suggests non-representative BAL for DPLD diagnosis.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: A high percentage of epithelial cells (>5%) is indicative for contamination by bronchial cells.

diagnostic_approaches.name: BAL cell viability acceptable range
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Quality control of recovered BAL cells.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Assess by trypan blue exclusion.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Viability within range supports reliable downstream analyses.
limitations: Washing procedures may increase viability but reduce total cells.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Immediately after cell recovery and processing.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Cell viability is assessed by trypan blue exclusion and should range from 80% to 95%.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Normal BAL differential reference ranges
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Reference for interpreting BAL cellular patterns.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Deviations suggest specific inflammatory or disease patterns.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Baseline comparison in any BAL interpretation.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Normal in BAL may be 80–90% alveolar macrophages (AMs), 5–15% lymphocytes, 1–3% polymorphonuclear neutrophils, 1% eosinophils, and < 1% mast cells

diagnostic_approaches.name: Smoking-related BAL cytologic changes
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Identify smoking effect on BAL interpretation.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Characteristic morphology may indicate smoking-related changes.
limitations: May affect cell size and morphology
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: The alveolar macrophages from smokers are larger than those in nonsmokers (threefold to fivefold increase) and show a characteristic morphology.

diagnostic_approaches.name: BAL lymphocytosis threshold for hypersensitivity pneumonitis
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Support suspicion of hypersensitivity pneumonitis (HP).
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: >50% lymphocytes generally raises suspicion for HP.
limitations: CD4/CD8 ratio in HP may be decreased
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: In ILD when HP is in differential diagnosis.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: BAL lymphocytosis >50% generally raises a suspicion for the diagnosis of hypersensitivity pneumonitis

diagnostic_approaches.name: BAL neutrophilia frequency in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Interpret neutrophil-predominant BAL in context of IPF.
criteria_or_scoring: Neutrophilia observed in 70–90% of IPF patients.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: BAL neutrophilia is common in IPF but non-specific.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: appropriate clinical setting is observed in the BAL of 70–90% of patients with IPF.

diagnostic_approaches.name: BAL eosinophilia threshold for eosinophilic pneumonia
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Support diagnosis of eosinophilic pneumonia.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: If eosinophils exceed 25%, consider eosinophilic pneumonia.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When BAL shows eosinophil predominance without asthma/parasitic infection.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: If eosinophilia exceeds 25%, eosinophilic pneumonia has to be considered

diagnostic_approaches.name: Langerhans’ cell histiocytosis BAL criterion
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Diagnose/suggest LCH using BAL immunophenotyping.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Identify by monoclonal antibodies against CD1a antigen or Langerin.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: More than 5% Langerhans’ cells supports LCH (can be non-specific in some diseases).
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: presence of more than 5% Langerhans’ cells in BAL, identified by monoclonal antibodies directed against the CD1a antigen or Langerin

diagnostic_approaches.name: Plasma cells in BAL interpretive criterion
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Suggest specific etiologies when plasma cells are present.
criteria_or_scoring: Plasma cells absent in normal BAL
if present with foamy macrophages and increased lymphocytes suggest HP or drug-induced lung disease.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Presence supports HP or drug-induced lung disease; differentials include COP and chronic eosinophilic pneumonia.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When plasma cells are identified on BAL cytology.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Plasma cells are not present in normal BAL. If found, together with foamy macrophages and increased lymphocyte count, HP or drug-induced lung disease has to be suggested.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Alveolar hemorrhage BAL diagnostic features
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Diagnose diffuse alveolar hemorrhage by BAL.
criteria_or_scoring: Increased intensity from fraction to fraction
Fragmented red blood cells in the alveolar macrophages
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Evaluate sequential BAL aliquots and cytology for RBCs and siderophages.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Combined features including ≥20% siderophages support alveolar hemorrhage.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When clinical/radiologic suspicion of alveolar hemorrhage exists.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: ≥20% siderophages

diagnostic_approaches.name: Pulmonary alveolar proteinosis BAL appearance
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Identify alveolar proteinosis via BAL cytology.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Assess gross appearance and apply PAS staining on stored slides.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Milky/turbid BAL with PAS+ material supports alveolar proteinosis.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Milky fluid, PAS + acellular corpuscles

diagnostic_approaches.name: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis BAL features (Table 1)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Support diagnosis of HP using BAL.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Elevated lymphocytes with low/variable CD4/CD8 support HP.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Lymphocytosis >25%

diagnostic_approaches.name: Sarcoidosis BAL features (Table 1)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Support diagnosis of sarcoidosis using BAL.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Elevated CD4/CD8 ratio supports sarcoidosis in appropriate context.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: CD4/CD8 ratio >3.5 (in the absence of mixed cellular pattern)

diagnostic_approaches.name: Asbestosis BAL feature
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Support diagnosis of asbestosis using BAL.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Elevated asbestos bodies support exposure-related disease.
limitations: Quantification methods may vary between centers.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Increased asbestos body count

diagnostic_approaches.name: Pneumoconiosis BAL features
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Identify dust-related lung disease using BAL.
criteria_or_scoring: Dust particles and birefringent material in alveolar macrophages.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Presence suggests pneumoconiosis in exposure context.
limitations: Findings depend on exposure and technique.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Dust particles in alveolar macrophages Birefringent material in alveolar macrophages

diagnostic_approaches.name: Lipoid pneumonia BAL features
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Support diagnosis of lipoid pneumonia.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Lipid-laden macrophages indicate lipoid aspiration/infiltration.
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When clinical suspicion of lipoid pneumonia exists.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Lipid-laden alveolar macrophages

diagnostic_approaches.name: Infectious disease diagnosis via BAL
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Detect pathogens in lower respiratory tract.
criteria_or_scoring: Infectious organisms by stains or cultures.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Perform complete microbiological assessment including cultures and special stains when indicated.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Presence confirms infection.
limitations: Contamination or inadequate sampling may affect yield.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Infectious organisms by stains or cultures

diagnostic_approaches.name: Malignant infiltration detection by BAL cytology
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Identify malignant cells in pulmonary infiltrates.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Add Papanicolaou stain if malignancy suspected; cytology review.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Detection supports malignant infiltration.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Malignant cells

diagnostic_approaches.name: BAL algorithm neutrophil threshold (Fig. 1)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Classify BAL pattern as neutrophilic.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Neutrophilic pattern suggests entities such as IPF, ARDS, infections (context-dependent).
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: neutrophilic GRANULOCYTES > 3 – 5 %

diagnostic_approaches.name: BAL algorithm eosinophil threshold (Fig. 1)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Classify BAL pattern as eosinophilic.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Suggests eosinophilic pneumonia, Churg-Strauss (clinical correlation required).
limitations: Requires exclusion of asthma and parasitic infections.
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: eosinophilic GRANULOCYTES > 25%

diagnostic_approaches.name: BAL algorithm lymphocyte thresholds (Fig. 1)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Classify BAL as lymphocytic and gauge degree.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: >50% may suggest HP; lower increases seen in sarcoidosis/others (context-dependent).
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: LYMPHOCYTES > 12- 15 % > 50 %

diagnostic_approaches.name: BAL algorithm CD4/CD8 ratio interpretation (Fig. 1)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Use CD4/CD8 ratio to support differential diagnoses.
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Determine lymphocyte subsets by flow cytometry/immunocytochemistry when indicated.
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Higher ratios may support sarcoidosis; lower ratios may support HP/EAA (context-dependent).

diagnostic_approaches.name: BAL cytology for pulmonary alveolar proteinosis (PAP)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Diagnose PAP using characteristic BAL cytology
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Light microscopy of BAL with May-Grünwald-Giemsa and PAS staining
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Virtually pathognomonic; obviates need for transbronchial or surgical lung biopsy
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: The combination of grossly milky BAL fluid, PAS-positive acellular oval bodies, and foamy macrophages…is virtually pathognomonic of the disease and obviates the need for…biopsy.

diagnostic_approaches.name: BAL cytology for pulmonary Langerhans’ cell histiocytosis (PLCH)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Support diagnosis of PLCH via BAL differential cytology
criteria_or_scoring: >5% Langerhans’ cells of total BAL cell count
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: BAL differential cytology
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Specific finding is increase in Langerhans’ cells to >5%
limitations: low proportions can be seen in other conditions
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: The specific finding is an increase in Langerhans’ cells to >5% of the total BAL cell count. The sensitivity is low…

diagnostic_approaches.name: Immunostaining (CD1a/Langerin) to identify Langerhans’ cells in BAL
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Identify Langerhans’ cells in BAL for PLCH assessment
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Staining by monoclonal antibodies for CD1a or Langerin
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Positive staining identifies Langerhans’ cells; S100 is less specific
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Staining by monoclonal antibodies for CD1a or Langerin enables identification of Langerhans’ cells in BAL. The reaction with the polyclonal antibody S100 is less specific.

diagnostic_approaches.name: BAL evaluation for diffuse alveolar hemorrhage (DAH) using siderophage percentage
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Diagnose/exclude DAH and assess severity
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: BAL with sequential fractions; count siderophages; may use Golde score
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Recovered fluid stains more intensely from fraction to fraction; first fraction bloodiest suggests bronchial aspiration
limitations: Hemosiderin-laden macrophages appear ≥48 h after bleeding
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Patients with unexplained pulmonary infiltrates to confirm/exclude DAH
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: …a percentage of siderophages ≥20% is sufficient for the diagnosis of DAH. Hemosiderin-laden macrophages do not appear earlier than 48 h after bleeding.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Golde score for DAH
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Assess severity of bleeding in DAH
criteria_or_scoring: Takes into account intensity of staining of each macrophage
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Apply Golde score on BAL macrophages
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: When detailed severity assessment is needed
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: …the time-consuming application of the Golde score, which also takes into account the intensity of staining of each macrophage.

diagnostic_approaches.name: BAL cytology for diffuse malignant infiltrates
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Diagnose diffuse malignant pulmonary infiltrates
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: BAL with cytology; may support hematologic malignancy diagnosis
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Reliable diagnosis achievable in many cases
limitations: Not as sensitive for solid tumors as biopsy or transbronchial needle aspiration
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: …diffuse malignant infiltrates can be reliably diagnosed in 60–90% of cases (Fig. 5).

diagnostic_approaches.name: Quantification of asbestos bodies in BAL by millipore filtration
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Support diagnosis/exposure assessment in asbestos-related disease
criteria_or_scoring: quantification by specific millipore filtration technique
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Specific millipore filtration to quantify asbestos bodies
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Good correlation with lung tissue asbestos body count
limitations: Negative BAL does not exclude disease
10–15% exposed have no detectable asbestos bodies
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: …10–15% of subjects with known occupational asbestos exposure do not have detectable asbestos bodies in their BAL fluid.

diagnostic_approaches.name: BAL criteria for eosinophilic lung diseases (acute/chronic eosinophilic pneumonia)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Diagnose eosinophilic lung diseases via BAL
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: BAL of radiologically affected segment
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: BAL supports diagnosis with clinical and HRCT findings; milder eosinophilia <20% has limited significance
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Eosinophilic lung diseases can be diagnosed when there are ≥25% eosinophils… the fraction… ranges from 20% to 90%…

diagnostic_approaches.name: BAL findings suggestive of aspiration (lipoid pneumonia)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Suggest diagnosis of lipoid pneumonia due to chronic aspiration
criteria_or_scoring: Large numbers of lipid-laden macrophages with marked vacuolization of cytoplasm
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: BAL analysis and cytology
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Highly suggestive for lipoid pneumonia
limitations: Differential diagnoses include hypersensitivity pneumonia and drug-induced pneumonia
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Recurrent pneumonia or atypical diffuse infiltrates
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: BAL analysis shows usually large numbers of lipid-laden macrophages with marked vacuolization of their cytoplasm.

diagnostic_approaches.name: BAL use in severe ARDS of unknown etiology
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Pursue cause of severe ARDS when etiology is unknown
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Consider performing BAL after weighing risks and benefits
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: …consider performing BAL in patients with severe ARDS of unknown etiology to pursue its cause [8].

diagnostic_approaches.name: BAL sensitivity for infections in immunocompromised patients
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Diagnose opportunistic and other infections using BAL
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Process BAL for bacterial, mycobacterial, fungal, and viral pathogens; cytology
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: High sensitivity for Pneumocystis; variable for others
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: The sensitivity of BAL ranges from 60% to 90%… 70–80%… and 90–95% in Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia.

diagnostic_approaches.name: PCR for Pneumocystis jirovecii on BAL
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Detect Pneumocystis jirovecii DNA in BAL
criteria_or_scoring: confirm positive PCR by staining to distinguish colonization vs infection
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: PCR on BAL; avoid filtering through gauze; use staining (e.g., Grocott) for confirmation
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: High sensitivity; positive PCR should be confirmed by staining
limitations: Colonization vs infection requires staining confirmation
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: There is a high sensitivity of PCR (>90%) for Pneumocystis jirovecii in BAL [28].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Cytologic identification of cytomegalovirus (CMV) in BAL
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Support diagnosis of CMV pneumonia
criteria_or_scoring: Cytomegalic-transformed cell (owl eye cell) with typical nuclear or cytoplasmic inclusions
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Light microscopy of BAL cytology
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Highly specific finding; seen in a proportion of cases
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: …the characteristic cytomegalic-transformed cell (the owl eye cell)… can be seen on light microscopy in 30–50% of cases.

diagnostic_approaches.name: BAL pattern suggestive of hypersensitivity pneumonitis (HP)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Support HP diagnosis via BAL cellular profile
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: BAL with differential cell counts and CD4/CD8 ratio
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Predominant lymphocytosis supports HP
limitations: Profile influenced by timing and exposure intensity
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: The proportion of lymphocytes exceeds often 50%.

diagnostic_approaches.name: BAL CD4/CD8 ratio threshold for sarcoidosis
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Support sarcoidosis diagnosis via BAL lymphocyte subset ratio
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: BAL with flow cytometry or immunophenotyping for CD4/CD8
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Higher ratio favors sarcoidosis (with variability)
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: CD4/CD8 ratio >3.5, but high variability

diagnostic_approaches.name: Diagnostic performance of BAL CD4/CD8 ratio in sarcoidosis
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Quantify sensitivity and specificity of CD4/CD8 ratio for sarcoidosis
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: BAL with CD4/CD8 ratio measurement
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Low sensitivity, high specificity
limitations: not every patient has increased ratio
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: The sensitivity… is low around only 55%, but the specificity is high around 95%…

diagnostic_approaches.name: BAL differential cell counts in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Support IPF diagnosis and differentiate from other ILDs
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: BAL with differential cell counts
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Pattern differs from sarcoidosis or HP; lymphocytosis uncommon
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Moderate increased neutrophil count (10–30%) in 70–90%… Eosinophils slightly increased (in 40–60%… ) Neutrophils >2× eosinophils

diagnostic_approaches.name: BAL profile suggestive of cryptogenic organizing pneumonia (COP)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Suggest COP using BAL cellular profile with clinical/radiologic context
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: BAL with differential and CD4/CD8 ratio
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Combination highly suggestive for COP
limitations: Requires exclusion of infection or malignancy
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: …>20% lymphocytes, eosinophils between 2% and 25%, and a CD4/CD8 ratio <1.0 are highly suggestive for COP…

diagnostic_approaches.name: BAL findings in acute interstitial pneumonia (AIP)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Support AIP diagnosis using BAL features
criteria_or_scoring: BAL fluid often bloody and rich in albumin
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: BAL with cytology
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Findings indicate increased alveolar capillary permeability and acute injury
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: The BAL fluid in acute interstitial pneumonia is often bloody and rich in albumin… marked increase in neutrophils…

diagnostic_approaches.name: BAL findings in smoking-related ILDs (DIP and RB/ILD)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Support diagnosis of DIP/RB-ILD in smokers
criteria_or_scoring: Increase in macrophages with black pigmented inclusions
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: BAL with cytology and differential counts
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Smoker BAL differs from normal with elevated macrophages
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: The typical BAL finding in desquamative interstitial pneumonia and RB/ILD is an increase in macrophages with black pigmented inclusions.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Lymphocyte transformation test (LTT) in BAL for chronic beryllium disease
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Confirm diagnosis of chronic beryllium disease
criteria_or_scoring: In vitro lymphocyte transformation to known antigen
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: LTT performed on BAL lymphocytes
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: More sensitive and specific than blood test
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Diagnosis can be confirmed by an in vitro lymphocyte transformation test… The transformation test in BAL is more sensitive and specific than the blood test…

diagnostic_approaches.name: Mini-BAL for pneumonia diagnosis
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Less invasive alternative sampling for pneumonia diagnosis
criteria_or_scoring: High sensitivity and specificity for pneumonia diagnosis
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Mini-BAL sampling with microbiologic workup
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Acceptable alternative to standard BAL
limitations: Often no advantage over less invasive procedures in many clinical situations
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: The sensitivity and the specificity of the mini-BAL for diagnosis of pneumonia are high, so mini-BAL could be considered as an acceptable alternative [41].

diagnostic_approaches.name: Quantitative culture thresholds for ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Differentiate colonization vs infection and diagnose VAP
criteria_or_scoring: Cutoff of ≥105 or ≥104 CFU/m L indicates VAP
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Quantitative culture of tracheal aspirations or BAL
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Counts above thresholds indicate VAP
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: The cutoff of ≥105 resp. ≥104 CFU/m L is accepted as an indicator for ventilator-associated pneumonia.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Legionella detection from BAL
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Diagnose Legionella infection
criteria_or_scoring: Detection by direct immunofluorescence or bacterial culture
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Direct immunofluorescence technique or culture on BAL
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Positive DFA or culture indicates infection
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Legionella infections can be detected either by direct immunofluorescence technique or by bacterial culture.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Galactomannan enzyme immunoassay on BAL
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Diagnose invasive aspergillosis via fungal antigen detection
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Enzyme immunoassay for galactomannan on BAL
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Positive antigen supports invasive aspergillosis
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Galactomannan enzyme immunoassay for fungal antigen detection is commonly used to diagnose invasive aspergillosis.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Metagenomic whole-genome sequencing (WGS) of BAL fluid
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Diagnose and manage viral, bacterial, and fungal pneumonias
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: Whole-genome sequencing, including real-time metagenomic sequencing, of BAL fluid
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Identifies pathogens directly from BAL
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Critically ill patients with and without immunosuppression
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: …whole-genome sequencing, including real-time metagenomic sequencing, of BAL fluid has been used to diagnose and manage viral, bacterial, and fungal pneumonias…

diagnostic_approaches.name: RT-PCR for SARS-Co V-2 with BAL when swabs are negative
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Diagnose COVID-19 when upper airway swabs are false negative
criteria_or_scoring: BAL may prove diagnostic in suspected cases with negative swabs
diagnostic_approaches.how_to_perform: RT-PCR on BAL fluid
diagnostic_approaches.interpretation: Positive RT-PCR confirms infection
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: Suspected COVID-19 with negative oropharyngeal/nasopharyngeal swabs
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: …in suspected cases, where these samples are false negative, BAL may prove diagnostic.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL)
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: diagnostic approach and management of diseases such as sarcoidosis, HP, or IPF
limitations: use of BAL is discussed controversially
fail to integrate BAL data with other clinical and radiological information
Further studies to assess the additional value of BAL are required
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: the diagnostic approach and management of more common diseases such as sarcoidosis, HP, or IPF. But this use of BAL is discussed controversially

diagnostic_approaches.purpose: classification of the idiopathic interstitial pneumonias
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: ATS/ERS international multidisciplinary consensus classification of the idiopathic interstitial pneumonias.

diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: patients with indeterminate for usual interstitial pneumonia imaging pattern
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Diagnostic value of BAL lymphocytosis in patients with indeterminate for usual interstitial pneumonia imaging pattern.

diagnostic_approaches.purpose: bronchoalveolar lavage diagnostics in critically ill patients
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Application of metagenomic next-generation sequencing for bronchoalveolar lavage diagnostics in critically ill patients.

diagnostic_approaches.purpose: detection of Mycoplasma pneumoniae in respiratory specimens
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Real-time PCR detection of Mycoplasma pneumoniae in respiratory specimens.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Multiplex and real-time PCR detection of herpes viruses in BAL fluid
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Detection of herpes viruses in BAL fluid
diagnostic_approaches.when_to_use: patients with acute lung injury or acute respiratory distress syndrome
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Detection of herpes viruses by multiplex and real-time polymerase chain reaction in bronchoalveolar lavage fluid of patients with acute lung injury or acute respiratory distress syndrome.

diagnostic_approaches.name: Vitamin E acetate test in BAL fluid
diagnostic_approaches.purpose: associated with EVALI
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Vitamin E acetate in bronchoalveolar-lavage fluid associated with EVALI.

diagnostic_approaches.purpose: Utility in pulmonary Langerhans cell histiocytosis
diagnostic_approaches.source_excerpt: Utility of bronchoscopy in pulmonary Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

diagnostic_approaches.purpose: use of bronchoalveolar lavage in hypersensitivity pneumonitis

treatment_algorithms.title: BAL diagnostic algorithm (cellular patterns and thresholds)
treatment_algorithms.condition: Diagnostic interpretation of BAL cellular patterns
specific_recommendations: LYMPHOCYTES > 12- 15 %
CD4/CD8 > 5
CD4/CD8 < 1
neutrophilic GRANULOCYTES > 3 – 5 %
eosinophilic GRANULOCYTES > 25 %
CD4/CD8 evaluation is valuable
decision_points_and_pathways: If LYMPHOCYTES > 12- 15 % and CD4/CD8 > 5 -> sarcoidosis, berylliosis, asbestosis, autoimmune disease
If LYMPHOCYTES with CD4/CD8 < 1 -> EAA, pneumoconiosis, drugs-induced, HIV, COOP
If neutrophilic GRANULOCYTES > 3 – 5 % -> EAA, IPF, ARDS, pneumonia, bronchitis
If eosinophilic GRANULOCYTES > 25% -> eosinophilic pneumonia, Churg Strauss

clinical_guidelines.title: Site selection for BAL in diffuse lung disease
clinical_guidelines.condition: Performing bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) in diffuse lung disease
specific_recommendations: The middle lobe or the lingula is recommended as standard site for BAL, if diffuse lung disease is present.
From these lobes, about 20% more fluid and cells are recovered than from the lower lobes.
clinical_guidelines.alternative_approaches: Alternatively, one of the anterior segments or subsegments of the upper or lower lobes may be used if standard site is impossible or difficult.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: From these lobes, about 20% more ﬂuid and cells are recovered than from the lower lobes.

clinical_guidelines.title: Target BAL to HRCT-identified affected segments
clinical_guidelines.condition: Interstitial lung disease with potential benefit from targeted BAL
specific_recommendations: Target BAL to one of the pulmonary segments most affected, as identified by chest HRCT not older than 6 weeks.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with diffuse lung disease undergoing BAL and HRCT available
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: as identiﬁed by chest high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) not older than 6 weeks.

clinical_guidelines.title: Preferred site for BAL in localized lesions
clinical_guidelines.condition: Patients with marked radiographic heterogeneity or localized lesions
specific_recommendations: Choose the area of greatest abnormality, as seen on chest radiograph or CT, as the preferred site for BAL.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with localized lesions or marked radiographic heterogeneity
clinical_guidelines.alternative_approaches: Some follow BAL at two or three different sites to reach higher representation.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: it is recommended that the area of greatest abnormality, as seen on the chest radiograph or CT, should be chosen as the preferred site for BAL.

clinical_guidelines.title: Multisite BAL for representation
specific_recommendations: Consider BAL at two or three different sites to reach higher representation.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Some follow the concept of BAL at two or three different sites to reach higher representation

clinical_guidelines.title: Instillate type for BAL
specific_recommendations: Use sterile isotonic saline solution (0.9% Na Cl) as the instillate.
Warming the instillate to body temperature may prevent coughing and increase cellular yield.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: The most commonly used instillate is sterile isotonic saline solution (0.9% Na Cl).

clinical_guidelines.title: BAL aliquots and total instilled volume
specific_recommendations: Use 20 m L syringes (alternatively 60 m L).
Instill four to five aliquots up to a total volume of 100–300 m L.
decision_points_and_pathways: Smaller instilled volumes risk contamination by the bronchial spaces.
clinical_guidelines.alternative_approaches: 60 m L syringes may be used as an alternative.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Commonly 20 m L syringes are used (alternatively 60 m L) and four to ﬁve aliquots are recommended up to a total instilled volume of 100–300 m L.

clinical_guidelines.title: Expected recovery volume in BAL
clinical_guidelines.condition: Assessing adequacy of BAL sample recovery
specific_recommendations: A recovery of 30–70% of the instilled volume is normal.
The minimum acceptable recovery is 5%, adequate for analysis.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: A recovery of 30–70% of the instilled volume is normal. The minimum is at 5%, which is adequate for analysis.

clinical_guidelines.title: Bronchoscopic positioning for optimal BAL recovery
clinical_guidelines.condition: Technique to optimize BAL fluid recovery
specific_recommendations: Occlude the bronchial lumen with the bronchoscope to accomplish optimal recovery.
Advance the bronchoscope tip into wedge position.
clinical_guidelines.alternative_approaches: A suction catheter through the working channel can be used, placed more peripherally.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Optimal recovery is accomplished by occluding the bronchial lumen with the bronchoscope.

clinical_guidelines.title: Remove local anesthesia fluid prior to BAL
specific_recommendations: Remove local anesthesia fluid prior to instillation of lavage fluid, since it may influence cell viability.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Local anesthesia ﬂuid should be removed prior to instillation of lavage ﬂuid, since it may inﬂuence cell viability.

clinical_guidelines.title: Recommended collection containers for BAL
specific_recommendations: Use siliconized or plastic containers to avoid loss of cells through adhesion to glass surfaces.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Siliconized or plastic containers are recommended to avoid loss of cells through adhesion to glass surfaces.

clinical_guidelines.title: Intra-procedural monitoring and oxygen during BAL
specific_recommendations: Provide supplemental oxygen throughout the entire procedure.
Use oximetry, ECG, and blood pressure monitoring.
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: Supplemental oxygen, oximetry, ECG and blood pressure monitoring are recommended.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Supplemental oxygen delivery throughout the entire procedure, oximetry, and ECG and blood pressure monitoring are recommended.

clinical_guidelines.title: Risk factor thresholds for major complications of BAL
clinical_guidelines.condition: Identifying patients at higher risk of major complications during BAL
specific_recommendations: Avoid BAL or exercise caution in presence of: p O2 < 8.0 k Pa (<60 mm Hg), SO2 < 90%, FEV1 < 1.0 L.
Bleeding disorders: prothrombin time <50 s, platelet counts <20,000 platelets/m L.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with severe lung or heart disease or significant comorbidity
clinical_guidelines.contraindications_and_exceptions: Relative contraindications include cardiopulmonary instability or severe hemorrhagic diathesis.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: p O2 < 8.0 k Pa (<60 mm Hg), SO2 < 90%, FEV1 < 1.0 L, bleeding disorders (prothrombin time <50 s, platelet counts <20,000 platelets/m L)

clinical_guidelines.title: Relative contraindications for BAL
clinical_guidelines.condition: Determining whether to proceed with BAL
specific_recommendations: BAL is contraindicated (relative) if the patient has cardiopulmonary instability or a severe hemorrhagic diathesis.
clinical_guidelines.contraindications_and_exceptions: Relative: cardiopulmonary instability or severe hemorrhagic diathesis.
clinical_guidelines.alternative_approaches: Absolute contraindications for BAL do not differ from those for bronchoscopy.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: BAL is contraindicated (relative) if the patient has cardiopulmonary instability or a severe hemorrhagic diathesis.

clinical_guidelines.title: Timely transport of BAL specimens
clinical_guidelines.condition: Post-procedure handling of BAL samples for laboratory processing
specific_recommendations: Transfer materials to the laboratory as quickly as possible, best within 1 h.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: It is essential that the transfer of the materials to the laboratory is performed as quickly as possible, best within 1 h.

clinical_guidelines.title: Centrifugation parameters for BAL samples
clinical_guidelines.condition: Laboratory processing of BAL fluid (cellular analyses)
specific_recommendations: Centrifuge for 10 min at 500 g.
clinical_guidelines.alternative_approaches: The supernatant can be stored frozen for subsequent analysis of soluble components.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: (3) centrifugation for 10 min at 500 g,

clinical_guidelines.title: Routine BAL analyses for ILD
clinical_guidelines.condition: Workup of BAL fluid in suspected interstitial lung disease (ILD)
specific_recommendations: Include total and differential cell counts, lymphocyte subsets, morphological appearances of cells.
Perform cultures and special stains for infection in appropriate clinical settings.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Routine processing of BAL ﬂuid cellular analyses for patients with ILD includes total and differential cell counts ... besides cultures and special stains for infection

clinical_guidelines.title: Cell viability assessment range for BAL
clinical_guidelines.condition: Quality metrics for BAL cellular analyses
specific_recommendations: Assess cell viability by trypan blue; it should range from 80% to 95%.
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: Viability check using trypan blue exclusion.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Cell viability is assessed by trypan blue exclusion and should range from 80% to 95%.

clinical_guidelines.title: Minimum cells for BAL differential counts
clinical_guidelines.condition: Ensuring reproducibility of BAL differential counts
specific_recommendations: Count at least 600 cells on cytocentrifuge or smear preparations after May-Grünwald-Giemsa staining.
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: Use appropriate staining and count threshold to reduce variability.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: For the enumeration of cell differentials, at least 600 cells are counted

clinical_guidelines.title: Avoid Diff-Quick for BAL mast cell assessment
clinical_guidelines.condition: Staining selection for BAL differential counting including mast cells
specific_recommendations: Do not use the Diff-Quick stain because it does not stain mast cells.
clinical_guidelines.contraindications_and_exceptions: Avoid Diff-Quick when mast cells assessment is needed.
clinical_guidelines.alternative_approaches: Use May-Grünwald-Giemsa; store slides for special stains as needed.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: The Diff-Quick stain should not be used because it does not stain mast cells.

clinical_guidelines.title: Epithelial cell contamination threshold in BAL
clinical_guidelines.condition: Determining representativeness of BAL for diffuse parenchymal lung disease
specific_recommendations: A high percentage of epithelial cells (>5%) indicates contamination by bronchial cells.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: BAL for diagnosis of diffuse parenchymal lung disease
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: Note but exclude ciliated or squamous epithelial cells from differential count.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: A high percentage of epithelial cells (>5%) is indicative for contamination by bronchial cells.

clinical_guidelines.title: Store unstained slides for special stains
clinical_guidelines.condition: Preservation of BAL samples for potential further testing
specific_recommendations: Store at least three unstained slides for special staining if clinically indicated.
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: Maintain unstained slides for iron, PAS, silver, toluidine blue, fat, Ziehl-Neelsen if indicated.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: At least three unstained slides should be stored

clinical_guidelines.title: Minimum cell number for flow cytometry on BAL
clinical_guidelines.condition: Flow cytometry testing on BAL specimens
specific_recommendations: Require ≥1 × 106 cells to perform an adequate flow cytometry test.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with high lymphocyte counts or suspected Langerhans’ cell histiocytosis or lymphoma
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: Ensure sufficient cell yield prior to flow cytometry.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: that ≥1 × 106 cells are required to perform an adequate test.

clinical_guidelines.title: ERS Task Force: Reporting acellular components in BAL
clinical_guidelines.condition: Measurement/reporting of acellular components from BAL fluid
specific_recommendations: Express acellular components as amounts per m L of recovered BAL fluid to facilitate comparison.
clinical_guidelines.monitoring_requirements: Follow ERS Task Force detailed information on soluble components measurement.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: These components should be expressed as amounts per m L of recovered BAL ﬂuid

clinical_guidelines.title: ATS guideline: BAL with lymphocyte cellular analysis in suspected hypersensitivity pneumonitis
clinical_guidelines.condition: Newly identified ILD with differential including nonfibrotic or fibrotic hypersensitivity pneumonitis
specific_recommendations: Perform BAL with lymphocyte cellular analysis.
clinical_guidelines.patient_population_criteria: Patients with newly identified ILD whose differential diagnosis includes nonfibrotic or fibrotic hypersensitivity pneumonitis
clinical_guidelines.alternative_approaches: Consider absolute neutrophil and eosinophil counts as they may be increased.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: the ATS guideline recommends or suggests BAL with lymphocyte cellular analysis in hypersensitivity pneumonitis

clinical_guidelines.title: Diagnosis and BAL — Alveolar hemorrhage criteria
specific_recommendations: Macroscopically bloody BAL.
Increased intensity from fraction to fraction.
Free red blood cells.
Hemosiderin-laden macrophages.
Fragmented red blood cells in the alveolar macrophages.
≥20% siderophages.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: ≥20% siderophages

clinical_guidelines.title: Diagnosis and BAL — Eosinophilic pneumonia threshold
specific_recommendations: Eosinophils >25%.
clinical_guidelines.contraindications_and_exceptions: Exclude asthma and parasitic infections per context in text for eosinophilic cellular pattern.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Eosinophils >25%

clinical_guidelines.title: Diagnosis and BAL — Hypersensitivity pneumonitis thresholds
clinical_guidelines.condition: Diagnosing hypersensitivity pneumonitis using BAL findings
specific_recommendations: Lymphocytosis >25%.
CD4/CD8 ratio decreased, but variable too.
clinical_guidelines.contraindications_and_exceptions: CD4/CD8 may be decreased, normal, or increased (variability noted in text).
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Lymphocytosis >25% CD4/CD8 ratio decreased, but variable too

clinical_guidelines.title: Diagnosis and BAL — Langerhans’ cell histiocytosis threshold
clinical_guidelines.condition: Diagnosing Langerhans’ cell histiocytosis via BAL immunomarkers
specific_recommendations: CD1a + or Langerin + Langerhans’ cells >5%.
clinical_guidelines.contraindications_and_exceptions: Finding can be unspecific in some other fibrotic diseases per text context.
clinical_guidelines.alternative_approaches: Identify by monoclonal antibodies directed against CD1a or Langerin.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: CD1a + or Langerin + Langerhans’ cells >5%

clinical_guidelines.title: Diagnosis and BAL — Sarcoidosis indicators
specific_recommendations: Lymphocytosis >25%, but milder; moderate lymphocyte count only.
CD4/CD8 ratio >3.5 (in the absence of mixed cellular pattern).
clinical_guidelines.contraindications_and_exceptions: CD4/CD8 ratio can be variable in sarcoidosis (noted elsewhere in text).
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: CD4/CD8 ratio >3.5 (in the absence of mixed cellular pattern)

clinical_guidelines.title: BAL-based diagnosis of pulmonary alveolar proteinosis
specific_recommendations: Combination of milky BAL fluid, PAS-positive acellular oval bodies, and foamy macrophages is pathognomonic and obviates biopsy.
If unclear, proceed to lung biopsy.
decision_points_and_pathways: If milky BAL + PAS-positive acellular oval bodies + foamy macrophages present → no biopsy needed.
If diagnosis remains unclear → perform lung biopsy.
alternative_approaches: Transbronchial or surgical lung biopsy if findings are unclear.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: PAS-positive acellular oval bodies, and foamy macrophages under light microscopy is virtually pathognomonic of the disease and obviates the need for transbronchial or surgical lung biopsy.

clinical_guidelines.title: BAL threshold for pulmonary Langerhans’ cell histiocytosis
specific_recommendations: Langerhans’ cells >5% of total BAL cell count supports diagnosis.
Use monoclonal antibodies for CD1a or Langerin to identify Langerhans’ cells.
S100 antibody is less specific.
decision_points_and_pathways: If BAL Langerhans’ cells >5% → supports PLCH.
contraindications_and_exceptions: S100 is less specific than CD1a/Langerin.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: The speciﬁc ﬁnding is an increase in Langerhans’ cells to >5% of the total BAL cell count.

clinical_guidelines.title: BAL confirmation and assessment of diffuse alveolar hemorrhage (DAH)
specific_recommendations: Numerous hemosiderin-laden macrophages on BAL support DAH.
Siderophages ≥20% is sufficient for DAH diagnosis.
Recovered BAL fluid staining intensity increases fraction-to-fraction in alveolar hemorrhage.
First fraction bloodiest suggests aspirated bronchial blood.
decision_points_and_pathways: If fraction-to-fraction staining increases → alveolar hemorrhage.
If first fraction is bloodiest → aspirated bronchial blood.
patient_population_criteria: Patients with unexplained pulmonary infiltrates when coagulopathy is excluded.
contraindications_and_exceptions: Hemosiderin-laden macrophages do not appear earlier than 48 h after bleeding.
alternative_approaches: Golde score (time-consuming) versus percent siderophages counting.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: It has been shown that a percentage of siderophages ≥20% is sufﬁcient for the diagnosis of DAH. Hemosiderin-laden macrophages do not appear earlier than 48 h after bleeding.

clinical_guidelines.title: BAL criteria for eosinophilic pneumonia
specific_recommendations: BAL eosinophils >25% (up to 90%).
Eosinophils > neutrophils.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Eosinophils >25% (up to 90%) Eosinophils > neutrophils

clinical_guidelines.title: BAL pattern and exclusions for hypersensitivity pneumonitis (HP)
specific_recommendations: Lymphocytosis >50% on BAL supports HP.
Exclusions for HP: normal cell appearance or isolated neutrophil or eosinophil increase.
decision_points_and_pathways: Following an acute HP episode, neutrophil count may increase transiently.
contraindications_and_exceptions: Normal cell appearance or isolated neutrophil/eosinophil increase excludes HP.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Lymphocytosis >50%

clinical_guidelines.title: Sarcoidosis BAL evaluation
specific_recommendations: CD4/CD8 ratio >3.5 may support sarcoidosis but has high variability.
Consider transbronchial lung biopsy.
Consider EBUS-TBNA.
decision_points_and_pathways: If BAL pattern equivocal → consider transbronchial lung biopsy or EBUS-TBNA.
alternative_approaches: EBUS-TBNA as an alternative diagnostic approach.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: CD4/CD8 ratio >3.5, but high variability Consider transbronchial lung biopsy Consider EBUS-TBNA

clinical_guidelines.title: BAL-derived suggestion for cryptogenic organizing pneumonia (COP)
specific_recommendations: BAL lymphocytes >20%, eosinophils 2–25%, CD4/CD8 <1.0 with typical clinical/radiology and exclusion of infection/malignancy is highly suggestive of COP.
decision_points_and_pathways: If infection or malignancy excluded and thresholds met → COP highly suggestive.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: a BAL cell proﬁle of >20% lymphocytes, eosinophils between 2% and 25%, and a CD4/CD8 ratio <1.0 are highly suggestive for COP if infection or malignancy is excluded [45].

clinical_guidelines.title: IPF BAL cell profile characteristics
specific_recommendations: Neutrophils 10–30% in 70–90% of patients.
Eosinophils slightly increased in 40–60% of patients.
Neutrophils >2× eosinophils.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: Moderate increased neutrophil count (10–30%) in 70–90% of patients Eosinophils slightly increased (in 40–60% of patients) Neutrophils >2× eosinophils

clinical_guidelines.title: Asbestos exposure assessment via BAL
specific_recommendations: Quantify asbestos bodies using millipore filtration (more sensitive).
Negative BAL asbestos body count does not exclude disease (10–15% exposed have no detectable bodies).
contraindications_and_exceptions: Negative BAL asbestos body count does not exclude disease.
alternative_approaches: Lung tissue analysis for asbestos body count.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: A negative BAL asbestos body count does not exclude asbestos-related disease, as 10–15% of subjects with known occupational asbestos exposure do not have detectable asbestos bodies in their BAL ﬂuid.

clinical_guidelines.title: Diagnosis of ventilator-associated pneumonia (VAP) using quantitative cultures
specific_recommendations: Use combination of clinical, radiological, and laboratory criteria and quantitative culture of tracheal aspirations or BAL.
Cutoff of ≥105 resp. ≥104 CFU/m L indicates VAP.
decision_points_and_pathways: Clinical/radiological/laboratory criteria: new infiltration, fever or hypothermia, leukocytosis or leukopenia, putrid tracheal secretions.
Quantitative culture thresholds determine infection vs colonization.
alternative_approaches: Tracheal aspiration quantitative cultures as alternative to BAL.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: The cutoff of ≥105 resp. ≥104 CFU/m L is accepted as an indicator for ventilator-associated pneumonia.

clinical_guidelines.title: Microbiologic workup of BAL for lower respiratory tract infections
clinical_guidelines.condition: Suspected bacterial, mycobacterial, fungal, and viral infections
specific_recommendations: Process BAL promptly.
Stain and culture quantitatively for bacteria using appropriate media.
Stain and culture for mycobacteria (including nontuberculous) and fungi.
Use PCR/molecular assays; galactomannan EIA for invasive aspergillosis.
contraindications_and_exceptions: Avoid delays to prevent contamination or missing anaerobes.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: BAL ﬂuid should be stained and cultured quantitatively for bacteria using appropriate media, stained and cultured for mycobacteria (including mycobacteria other than M. tuberculosis) and for fungi.

clinical_guidelines.title: Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP) testing using BAL
specific_recommendations: Do not filter BAL fluid through gauze when PJP suspected.
PCR sensitivity >90% for Pneumocystis in BAL.
Confirm positive PCR by staining to distinguish colonization vs infection.
decision_points_and_pathways: If PJP suspected → avoid gauze filtration; use cytologic stains; PCR; confirm positive PCR by staining.
alternative_approaches: May-Grünwald-Giemsa, Grocott, modified toluidine blue, or silver methenamine stains.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: There is a high sensitivity of PCR (>90%) for Pneumocystis jirovecii in BAL [28].

clinical_guidelines.title: Consider BAL in severe ARDS of unknown etiology
specific_recommendations: After weighing risks and benefits, consider performing BAL to pursue the cause.
patient_population_criteria: Patients with severe ARDS of unknown etiology.
contraindications_and_exceptions: Consider risks and benefits before performing BAL.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: it would be worthwhile to consider performing BAL in patients with severe ARDS of unknown etiology to pursue its cause

clinical_guidelines.title: Chronic beryllium disease: BAL lymphocyte transformation test
specific_recommendations: Confirm diagnosis with in vitro lymphocyte transformation test.
BAL transformation test is more sensitive and specific than blood test.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: The transformation test in BAL is more sensitive and speciﬁc than the blood test [5].

clinical_guidelines.title: Use of BAL in suspected SARS-Co V-2 when upper airway tests are negative
specific_recommendations: If oropharyngeal/nasopharyngeal RT-PCR is suspected false negative, BAL may prove diagnostic.
Use BAL to diagnose additional cases and superadded infections in severe lower respiratory tract infection.
patient_population_criteria: Suspected SARS-Co V-2 with negative upper airway swabs.
Patients with severe COVID-19 lower respiratory tract infection.
alternative_approaches: Oropharyngeal and nasopharyngeal RT-PCR as gold standard.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: in suspected cases, where these samples are false negative, BAL may prove diagnostic.

clinical_guidelines.title: BAL findings suggestive of lipoid pneumonia due to aspiration
specific_recommendations: Large numbers of lipid-laden macrophages with marked cytoplasmic vacuolization are highly suggestive of lipoid pneumonia from chronic aspiration.
patient_population_criteria: Differential diagnosis of recurrent pneumonia or atypical diffuse pulmonary infiltrates.
alternative_approaches: Consider hypersensitivity pneumonia and drug-induced pneumonia as differentials.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: This ﬁnding is highly suggestive for lipoid pneumonia caused by chronic aspiration.

clinical_guidelines.title: Mini-BAL as an acceptable alternative for pneumonia diagnosis
specific_recommendations: Mini-BAL has high sensitivity and specificity and could be considered an acceptable alternative.
alternative_approaches: Standard BAL or tracheal aspirations with quantitative culture.
clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: The sensitivity and the speciﬁcity of the mini-BAL for diagnosis of pneumonia are high, so mini-BAL could be considered as an acceptable alternative [41].

clinical_guidelines.source_excerpt: The existing American Thoracic Society (ATS)/European Respiratory Society (ERS) consensus statement suggests different criteria for the clinical diagnosis of IPF including BAL [4].

problems_observed.finding: Inter-center variability in BAL results suggesting inconsistent adherence to standardized protocols
problems_observed.details: The chapter notes 'variability between centers,' emphasizing the need to 'follow standard protocols' to improve interpretability of BAL results.

problems_observed.finding: Lack of full standardization across key procedural steps despite existing guidelines
problems_observed.details: Instilled volume, patient positioning, suction, and processing 'have not been standardized totally,' contributing to differing results between laboratories and centers. Recommendations vary (e.g., 100–300 m L total volume; 20–50 m L aliquots).

problems_observed.finding: Practical conditions often diverge from ideal recommendations
problems_observed.details: Ideal conditions under general anesthesia with rigid or endotracheal intubation are 'far from daily routine.' Local anesthesia may interfere with recovered fluid and provoke cough, potentially affecting sample quality.

guideline_adherence.implication: Non-standardized BAL technique and variability in practice can compromise diagnostic consistency and accuracy, risking misinterpretation and misdiagnosis. Adherence to standardized protocols and expert, context-aware interpretation are essential to ensure reliable results and appropriate patient management.

technology_and_technique.topic: BAL procedural technique (instillation volume, aliquots, delivery)
technology_and_technique.summary: Minimum instilled volume about 100 mL in adults; recommendations range 100–300 mL delivered in 20–50 mL aliquots via bronchoscope in wedge position or via a more distal catheter. Performed under local anesthesia with moderate sedation; feasible in ventilated patients with special ventilator settings.
technology_and_technique.reference: Stanzel F, Tannapfel A. Bronchoalveolar Lavage. In: Principles and Practice of Interventional Pulmonology. Springer Nature Switzerland; 2025. doi:10.1007/978-3-031-49583-0_23-1

technology_and_technique.topic: Sampling site optimization for diffuse lung disease
technology_and_technique.summary: Middle lobe or lingula recommended as standard BAL site in diffuse lung disease; approximately 20% more fluid and cellular recovery from these lobes. Thinner bronchoscopes can access segments/subsegments to optimize sampling.
technology_and_technique.reference: Stanzel F, Tannapfel A. 2025. Bronchoalveolar Lavage. doi:10.1007/978-3-031-49583-0_23-1

technology_and_technique.topic: BAL vs bronchial washing vs whole-lung lavage (technique distinctions)
technology_and_technique.summary: BAL targets alveolar spaces with 100–300 mL total instillate, versus bronchial washing sampling large airways using ~20 mL primarily for microbiology/cytology. Whole-lung lavage is therapeutic for alveolar proteinosis under general anesthesia with repeated ~1000 mL instillations totaling >20 L.
technology_and_technique.reference: Stanzel F, Tannapfel A. 2025. Bronchoalveolar Lavage. doi:10.1007/978-3-031-49583-0_23-1; ref. [30]

technology_and_technique.summary: BAL is a low-risk, minimally invasive procedure typically done under local anesthesia with moderate sedation. Local anesthesia reduces cough but may contaminate recovered fluid and can itself provoke cough. Ideal conditions (general anesthesia via rigid or endotracheal tube) are not routine.
technology_and_technique.reference: Stanzel F, Tannapfel A. 2025. Bronchoalveolar Lavage. doi:10.1007/978-3-031-49583-0_23-1

technology_and_technique.topic: Diagnostic indications and potential to avoid surgical lung biopsy
technology_and_technique.summary: BAL can establish diagnoses in select conditions—alveolar hemorrhage, alveolar proteinosis, bronchioloalveolar carcinoma, Langerhans cell histiocytosis, and Pneumocystis pneumonia—potentially obviating surgical lung biopsy. Diagnostic usefulness is limited in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis; primary value is excluding alternatives such as sarcoidosis or hypersensitivity pneumonitis.
technology_and_technique.reference: Stanzel F, Tannapfel A. 2025. Bronchoalveolar Lavage. doi:10.1007/978-3-031-49583-0_23-1

technology_and_technique.summary: Compared to sputum analysis, BAL provides targeted lower respiratory tract sampling with less contamination from the upper aerodigestive tract, improving diagnostic accuracy for lower airway processes.
technology_and_technique.reference: Stanzel F, Tannapfel A. 2025. Bronchoalveolar Lavage. doi:10.1007/978-3-031-49583-0_23-1

technology_and_technique.summary: Inter-center variability in BAL results arises from differences in instilled volume, patient positioning, suction, and laboratory processing. Adherence to standardized protocols is emphasized to improve comparability and interpretability.
technology_and_technique.reference: Stanzel F, Tannapfel A. 2025. Bronchoalveolar Lavage. doi:10.1007/978-3-031-49583-0_23-1

technology_and_technique.topic: Patient selection and integration with imaging/clinical data
technology_and_technique.summary: Decision to perform BAL should be guided by clinical and radiologic presentation, patient status, and local expertise (both procedural and interpretive). BAL findings should be interpreted by experts in conjunction with HRCT and clinical context; even when nondiagnostic, cellular analysis helps narrow the differential.
technology_and_technique.reference: Stanzel F, Tannapfel A. 2025. Bronchoalveolar Lavage. doi:10.1007/978-3-031-49583-0_23-1

technology_and_technique.summary: BAL has a role in diagnosing bacterial pneumonia, tuberculosis, mycoses, and viral infections through targeted lower respiratory tract sampling, offering improved diagnostic material compared with non-directed specimens.
technology_and_technique.reference: Stanzel F, Tannapfel A. 2025. Bronchoalveolar Lavage. doi:10.1007/978-3-031-49583-0_23-1

technology_and_technique.summary: Instill sterile 0.9% NaCl warmed to body temperature in 20–50 mL aliquots to a total of 100–300 mL with the bronchoscope wedged; expected recovery 30–70% (≥5% minimally adequate). Remove local anesthetic before BAL; consider discarding first aliquot to reduce bronchial contamination. Use gentle suction and visual control to minimize mucosal trauma and collapse.

details.site_selection: Middle lobe/lingula for diffuse disease; HRCT-targeted abnormal segment for focal disease; multi-site in heterogeneous disease

lab_processing.differential_count: ≥600 cells; May–Grünwald–Giemsa; avoid Diff-Quick for mast cells

points: 13 Abstract Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) plays an important role in the diagnostic evaluation of interstitial lung disease, pul- monary inﬁltrates, and some infectious diseases as a min- imally invasive procedure

The decision to perform BAL should be guided by clinical and radiological presentation and the patient’s status as well as local technical expertise, both in performing the procedure and in interpreting the results
An important problem with interpreting BAL results is the variability between centers, which highlights the importance of following standard protocols
